result.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
result.summary: AI agents for autonomous scientific discovery must decide which experiments to run under a limited budget. Most benchmarks for science agents provide fixed datasets, while others that support active experimentation largely rely on simulation. We introduce Autonomous Science Bench, an initial release comprising six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns grounded in published experiments across biology, chemistry, and materials science. Agents select batches of designs, receive measurements from a lab service, and use the results to guide subsequent experiments before delivering a predictive model. Success requires passing two calibrated gates: a discovery gate, which evaluates the designs the agent measured, and a learning gate, which evaluates its model's ranking of held-out designs. In a pilot evaluation of eight agent-model configurations and 144 trials, the best configuration succeeds in 67% of trials, while the hardest campaign is solved in only three of 24 attempts. The two gates reveal different weaknesses: some agents build accurate rankings but find too few promising designs, while others find promising designs but fail to predict which unseen designs will perform well. These differences are obscured by overall success rates alone. We release version 0.1 of the campaigns, lab runtime, and public leaderboard at https://yibow.me/autonomous-science-bench.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Autonomous Science Bench，含六个有限预算的 design-build-test-learn 实验 campaign，让智能体选择批次设计、依据实测结果迭代，并用 discovery gate 与 learning gate 双重门槛分别评价其测量设计与对未观测设计的排序预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其双门槛设计把「找到有前景对象」与「预测未见对象」分开评价，可能为区分 LVR 中 latent 状态是真正支撑证据获取还是仅拟合答案提供评价思路；预算下的实验批次选择与何时继续测量也有类于 THINK/LOOK/STOP 决策，可供核查，但该工作本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理，属较远领域的启发线索。
